title: Write the autonomous sequence
summary: Load the two paths and put the drive, wait, aim and shoot commands in order.

say.never:
`Autos.java` holds the routine, and its constructor has two jobs: tell the routine which paths it uses, then list the commands to run.

The routine you will write runs these, one after another: drive the first path, wait a moment (a stand-in for picking up the game piece), drive the second path, aim until the robot is aimed (with a time limit), then shoot (also with a time limit).

You are done when Verify says the paths are named and the sequence is written. It reads your Java, so if a check fails its message says which line it wanted.
say.bit: Load the two paths, then list the commands: path, wait, path, aim until aimed (with a timeout), shoot (with a timeout).

say.never: A routine has to **load** a path before it can play it back. The name goes in quotes and must be exactly the name of the path in Choreo. One load for each path.

say.never:
The second job is the list of commands. Everything inside `addCommands(...)` runs **one after another**, with commas between the commands, each on its own line.

To drive a path, use the drivetrain's `followPath` command with the loaded path: it plays the path back and finishes when the robot has arrived. To wait, use `Commands.waitSeconds`: it does nothing for the time you give it, half a second here.
say.bit: addCommands runs its commands in order, separated by commas. followPath finishes on arrival; waitSeconds just waits.

say.never:
The aim command from the Computer Vision lesson never finishes by itself: it aims for as long as it runs. So it needs an **end**.

`.until(...)` ends it as soon as a yes/no method says true. Give it your `isAimed` method from the Computer Vision lesson. A `::` hands over the method itself, so the command can ask it again and again instead of asking once.

If something is wrong the robot might never become aimed, and the routine would be stuck forever. `.withTimeout(...)` gives up after a number of seconds. The shoot command never finishes either, so a timeout on it ends the routine. The last command has **no comma** after it.
say.bit: Aim never finishes alone: end it with until(isAimed) and give up with a timeout. Shoot also needs a timeout. No comma after the last command.
